scope: Narrow assertion-quality follow-up for the implemented ISO 32000-2:2020 §12.3.3 outline feature, focusing on Count/open-state consumers and Table 151 color/style actually reaching the public panel. This is not a whole-clause certification.

source.locator: General12.3.3 physical459/444; Table150 physical460/445; Table151 C/F physical461/446. Parent verified exact C row and root Count conditional.
source.ec3: No relevant changed EC3 outline annotation was identified in the prior effective-source check. The optional `/F` style flag's specified bits and `/C` DeviceRGB/default are in the base text.
source.requirements: §12.3.3 says items at a level appear in linked-list order, open children become visible, closed descendants are hidden, a visible item activates its destination/action, and users may open/close items. Table 151 item Count sign represents open/closed and its positive magnitude is the recursively computed number of visible descendants; leaf Count is omitted. Table 151 `/C` specifies DeviceRGB text color, default black; `/F` plus Table 152 bits 1 and 2 specify italic and bold. These are screen presentation semantics for a processor that displays the outline; the clause does not require every implementation to have a panel.

features.source_location: Printed pp.444–445 (physical pp.459–460): open/closed sign, visible descendants, recursively counted positive item Count, and hidden descendants under a closed item.
features.assertion_quality: Strong and independently triangulated. The exact-xref UI fixture has positive-count open parent and nested child, negative-count closed child with its own grandchild, a sibling after that branch, checks computed root visible_count=5, asserts initial depth-first visible row order and item identities, then toggles the closed child to reveal/hide its descendant without shifting identity. It also checks no recovery. The model/corpus test separately applies the clause algorithm to producer counts; known count disagreements are producer inconsistencies, not a reader-error requirement.
features.verdict: Covered for recursive count/open-state interpretation and the viewer-ui panel consumer. The panel is a product choice; do not turn producer validity constraints on matching stored count into mandatory reader rejection.

assertions: crates/pdf-model/src/outline.rs outline item decoding tests assert explicit `[1,0,0]` and default black
crates/viewer-ui/tests/panel.rs panel raster tests use outline items, but the shared `item` helper supplies only default black
features.assertion_quality: The parser-level value has a positive test, and the public consumer maps all three components into the text paint. Existing panel output assertions prove that outline ink is rendered, but do not pass a non-default outline color or discriminate default-black behavior at the drawn output. The prior §12.3.3 shard's assertion label 'outline rendering tests' should not be read as visual verification of `/C`.
features.verdict: Concrete assertion gap, not a demonstrated runtime defect. Draft `drafts/outline_colour_reaches_panel_pixels.rs` is an exact-xref public-consumer control: same title in explicit red and omitted-/C black items, parser checks, no-recovery check, and independent red-dominant pixel count in the rendered first row versus zero in the black control. No claim about exact glyph outlines or antialiasing.
features.parent_result: New exact-xref source-to-Sidebar CPU raster control PASS: red ink in first row, actual black ink in second title region, no red in default row.

features.source_location: Printed pp.445–446 (physical pp.460–461): `/F` bits are numbered low to high; bit 1 italic, bit 2 bold, all other bits shall be zero.
assertions: crates/pdf-model/src/outline.rs::reads_an_outline_item and associated item assertions cover flag decode
crates/pdf-script/tests/hook.rs::the_bookmark_root_walks_the_outline_a_person_sees_and_execute_asks_the_host checks script-facing style numeric value, not visual row font
crates/viewer-ui/tests/panel.rs does not set non-default bold/italic in its outline helper
features.assertion_quality: The data mapping is asserted in the model and the script-facing projection. I found no assertion that an actual sidebar rendered outline with `/F 1` or `/F 2` selects the corresponding face. Existing generic panel ink assertions cannot distinguish style flags.
features.verdict: Limited visual-assertion gap; no runtime failure demonstrated. ADR 0144 says the outline screen's style bits and `/C` are done, which is supported by the code path but its test claim needs to distinguish parser/script model evidence from a rendered-output oracle. I did not draft a font-shape test because font substitution/pixel geometry needs a carefully bounded independent oracle; the color case is cleaner.
